name: How do I remodel an older Pasadena or Glendale home without losing character?

mainEntity.name: How do I remodel an older Pasadena or Glendale home without making it look too modern or stripping away the original character?
mainEntity.text: How do I remodel an older Pasadena or Glendale home without making it look too modern or stripping away the original character?

acceptedAnswer.text: Older homes in Pasadena and Glendale often have architectural details that should guide the remodel instead of being erased by it. Character can usually be preserved by keeping original proportions, trim, built-ins, doors, millwork, and other elements that fit the home’s style. At the same time, the space may need better lighting, more storage, improved flow, and updated kitchens or baths to function for modern living. The best remodels do both: they modernize use without flattening the home’s identity. That usually means choosing finishes that complement the era of the house, avoiding overly trendy materials, and upgrading systems discreetly. A designer or contractor with older-home experience can help decide what to preserve, restore, or replace so the home feels current but still authentic.
acceptedAnswer.description: The best way to preserve character is to keep the home’s architectural details that still work, then update layout, lighting, storage, and worn finishes around them. Original trim, windows, built-ins, and proportions often define the style. Matching new materials to the era of the home creates a more seamless result.
